execution.progress: extract and inspect take one round; sowing is two paid one-round phases whose work, reserved seeds and patch persist; resume pays only the remaining phase after rechecks; rooting and growth run only in ordinary simulation.

details.costs: Study: 4 rounds, 0.2 energy each. extract: target your own whole untreated berry item; one unit per attempt (quantity 1): 1 round, 0.5 energy. inspect: x, y a site in reach and/or target your own item or a sowing patch in reach: 1 round, 0.2 energy. sow: target your seed lot; x, y a site in reach on open ordinary soil (.), moisture 0.3-1.2, waterlogging at most 0.1, 0.6 m clear of objects and people, fewer than 3 berry plants or patches being sown within 5 m. 2 rounds of 1 energy: loosen the patch, then place and cover the seeds; a loosened patch left by cancelled work needs only the second. pause, resume (workId), cancel: no energy. Refusals and failed rechecks cost nothing. No tool, vessel, water or soil is supplied.
details.effects: A whole berry unit (0.2 kg, food 8) is crushed: 0.01 kg of seeds (5 %, no food, no ageing) and 0.19 kg of pulp with all its food and age; both keep origin, harvest round and decay. The seeds of one unit are the one propagule the plant rules give one fruit unit; viability is unknown until something emerges. A unit whose parent is not a living berry plant has no represented seed: a paid failure, all pulp. Sowing moves the seeds from your inventory into the patch record, covered 5 mm deep in soil loosened 0.03 m. The patch gains establishment only from actual temperature (none at 6 C or below, full from 20 C), light, soil moisture (full from 0.6) and season; cold, darkness, drought or waterlogging stall it. At 12 a rooted seedling appears with no fruit (stock at most 4, the parent plant interval); fruit grows only under the existing growth rule; anyone may gather it. Watering a rooted plant is rooted-plant-watering. An unworked round pauses; cancel returns unsown seeds once and leaves loosened soil; death leaves them where you died. No reward or refund.

packet.access: Omission is not absence. Query abilities, own inventory, knowledge, projects, memory, state or personally observed objects in batches. Ability search/list returns compact catalogue entries; use exact ids for full interface details and applicability. Search results are indexes. Exact queries return one record per offset. All paged records use600-code-unit fragments with zero-based part0..parts-1, consistently in proactive and queried views. Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Queries do not perform physical trials or award experience. Exact-id queries return a complete record of up to 6000 code units as one value in a single result; larger records keep the paged form. Paged records omit their per-record notes: concatenate all parts before parsing; continue with the same exact id. Work records marked settled are completed, stopped or cancelled and show only identity, ability, mode, status, target, products and last payment; an exact state query with the same key returns the complete record. observation.terrain rows are "y:x:cells" strings: each character of cells is the terrain kind of one visible cell, at x, x+1, ... in row y. abilities.baseline entries with id, function and args summarize interfaces you neither used in the last 25 rounds nor need now. args lists the arguments in order: a bare name is a string; otherwise its type with any bounds (number>=lo, integer<=hi, integer lo..hi, and a bare lo..hi is a number range) or its choices a|b; ? marks an optional argument and "" means none. An exact abilities query by id returns the complete contract, including references and string limits of 200 or more code units.
